_provenance: Advisory review r9 of project-concept.md by codex gpt-5.5/xhigh, 2026-07-05, piloting the price-tag contrast contract (no validator existed yet), under the operator scope-freeze. r9 reviewed the note AS OF commit 7c1cf8c. Its single P2 (the r8 version rule over-corrected: rename_display_name preserves version, test-pinned) was conceded and fixed by DELEGATING to per-operation store behavior instead of stating any blanket rule. Historic first: the contrast table itself flagged I3 as SPECULATIVE — the blanket bump rule had no nameable victim — the first speculative verdict of the pilot series, emitted against the very note that designed the verdict. 12 invariants. Earlier pilots (r2-r8) in git history.

findings.summary: The r8 version correction is now over-broad. The note says work-area `version` is bumped on EVERY record change (`implementation/brainstorming/project-concept.md:165`) and the r8 pilot repeats that as the conceded fix (`implementation/brainstorming/project-concept-pricing-pilot.json:2`), but Agent99 has a real stored-record change that does not bump version: `rename_display_name` preserves version (`/Users/siddhartha/Development/source/life_prod/agent_99/apps/agent_99/lib/agent_99/body/work_area_store.ex:181`, `/Users/siddhartha/Development/source/life_prod/agent_99/apps/agent_99/lib/agent_99/body/work_area_store.ex:530`) and the test pins a display-name rename at version 1 (`/Users/siddhartha/Development/source/life_prod/agent_99/apps/agent_99/test/agent_99/body/work_area_store_test.exs:115`, `/Users/siddhartha/Development/source/life_prod/agent_99/apps/agent_99/test/agent_99/body/work_area_store_test.exs:124`). Since expected-state delivery exposes `version` while display_name is only the UI label (`/Users/siddhartha/Development/source/life_prod/agent_99/apps/agent_99_workspace/test/agent_99_workspace/executor_channel_test.exs:514`, `/Users/siddhartha/Development/source/life_prod/agent_99/apps/agent_99/lib/agent_99/body/work_area_store.ex:182`), a drafter can make label edits look like lifecycle/provenance changes to future executor consumers instead of Agent99-compatible label-only edits.

invariants_contrast.statement: A project is a generic named ecosystem spanning repositories or roots; runs bind to a project and work area rather than a single workspace path.

consumer.answer: Operators, launch flow, workers receiving project context, and future Agent99 adapters consume this boundary.

payload.answer: The project record carries policy, work_areas, and optional defaults.

frequency.answer: Low-frequency configuration, resolved at run init.

victim.answer: Cross-repo product work is harmed if reuse law stays per-run or per-path and misses ecosystem sources.

cost.answer: Adds project CRUD, project/work-area resolution, prompt plumbing, and ledger fields.

cheaper_alternative.answer: Keep the single workspace path; rejected because the motivating duplication was ecosystem-scoped.

ecosystem_equivalent.answer: gap: current orchestrator state stores one workspace path, not project/work-area addressing.

invariants_contrast.statement: Orchestrator project maps to Agent99 workspace, orchestrator work_areas map to Agent99 work areas, and current API workspace must become or alias primary_root.

consumer.answer: The future Agent99 adapter, Brain-facing vocabulary, run launcher, and machine API clients consume this mapping.

payload.answer: Agent99 workspace is the autonomy/policy boundary; work area is a named set of explicit roots.

frequency.answer: Read during project-bound launch and every machine API response exposing the current path vocabulary.

victim.answer: The adapter and operator are harmed if a repo path is mistaken for the Agent99 workspace boundary.

cost.answer: Requires stable project/work-area handles, schema wording, a primary_root alias, and compatibility tests.

cheaper_alternative.answer: Keep calling the repo path workspace; rejected because it preserves the naming collision.

ecosystem_equivalent.answer: adopt: Agent99 already defines workspace and work-area architecture; gap: current service launch still takes a path-shaped workspace.

invariants_contrast.statement: Work-area raw records carry Agent99's full stored domain; the note currently says version bumps on EVERY record change.

consumer.answer: Agent99 WorkAreaStore, executor expected-state delivery, launch resolution, and future fusion consume the record and version.

payload.answer: The raw value carries name, display_name, primary, additional, executor_id, version, and status.

frequency.answer: Read at launch, listing, inspection, and expected-state delivery; bounded by configured work areas.

victim.answer: Executor expected-state consumers need material descriptor/status/provenance versions; no victim is named for display-name-only version bumps.
victim.evidence: derived: expected-state maps carry version, while display_name is only a UI label and Agent99 preserves version on rename.

cost.answer: Requires exact Agent99-compatible validation and tests for material bumps plus the display_name exception.

cheaper_alternative.answer: Use Agent99's narrower version rule; rejected only for stale descriptor/status/provenance changes, not for UI-label edits.

ecosystem_equivalent.answer: reject: Agent99 does not bump display-name-only changes; it preserves the version.

invariants_contrast.statement: refs/work_area:<name> records are raw Agent99-readable maps, not KV envelopes, and raw-family concurrency CASes the entire current value.

consumer.answer: Agent99 WorkAreaStore, future fusion, and any local raw-family writer consume this storage split.

payload.answer: The raw value is the top-level work-area map; concurrency uses client.cas(key, current_value, new_value).

frequency.answer: Low-frequency work-area CRUD and executor transition paths; bounded by configured work areas.

victim.answer: The future Agent99 reader is harmed if raw work areas are enveloped or CASed against a domain version token instead of the current value.

cost.answer: Requires a separate raw-family path, whole-value CAS discipline, and compatibility tests.

cheaper_alternative.answer: Use one enveloped JSON store for all families; rejected because Agent99 reads work areas raw.

ecosystem_equivalent.answer: adopt: Agent99 already provides the raw record domain and whole-value CAS path.

invariants_contrast.statement: Raw work-area delete writes Agent99's tombstone {name, deleted: true, version} with positive version, prior version + 1.

consumer.answer: Agent99 WorkAreaStore, list filtering, point reads, and future fusion consume this tombstone shape.

payload.answer: The tombstone carries only name, deleted true, and version; WorkAreaStore recognizes it only when version is greater than zero.

frequency.answer: Low-frequency work-area delete path; bounded by operator CRUD actions.

victim.answer: The operator and future adapter are harmed if a deleted work area reads back as malformed instead of unknown/deleted.

cost.answer: Requires reading the prior record before delete, computing version + 1, and testing positive tombstones.

cheaper_alternative.answer: Write the generic envelope tombstone; rejected because Agent99 does not read envelopes for work areas.

ecosystem_equivalent.answer: adopt: WorkAreaStore already writes and recognizes this tombstone shape.

invariants_contrast.statement: Our work_area_meta, policy, and run families use the LPC-style CAS envelope; raw work areas do not.

consumer.answer: The project store, service, panel, future fusion pump, and future Brain visibility mirror consume this storage split.

payload.answer: The stored envelope carries revision, value, and deleted?; public reads carry exists?, revision, and value.

frequency.answer: Low-frequency project edits plus bounded status/digest projection writes during runs.

victim.answer: The operator and future Brain are harmed if fusion needs migration or loses projected run visibility.

cost.answer: Adds local KV, revision/CAS semantics, tombstones, serialization discipline, and tests.

cheaper_alternative.answer: A plain JSON file is cheaper; rejected because fusion is meant to be a transport swap.

ecosystem_equivalent.answer: adopt: LPC provides Client and Cas contracts; gap: the orchestrator lacks local project KV.

invariants_contrast.statement: Key grammar uses one reserved namespace for our families, while refs/work_area:<name> is Agent99-native and never namespaced; citations and verifier paths must stay inside work-area roots.

consumer.answer: The project store, future fusion pump, verifier, and prompt-driven workers consume the key and path-containment rules.

payload.answer: Families include raw work_area, work_area_meta, policy, run status, and reserved run digest keys; paths must land inside a work-area root.

frequency.answer: Every project-store access and every mechanical verifier path/citation check.

victim.answer: The operator is harmed if verifier paths escape granted roots or if future fusion hides work areas from Agent99's fixed reader.

cost.answer: Requires key builders, root containment checks, namespace configuration, and collision tests.

cheaper_alternative.answer: Ad hoc keys and filesystem paths are cheaper; rejected because they are collision-prone and can escape the work area.

ecosystem_equivalent.answer: adopt: LPC provides binary key primitives and refs helpers; gap: the project namespace/key grammar is new.

invariants_contrast.statement: Safeguards are versioned policy objects that add required contract fields, not prose-only warnings.

consumer.answer: Prompt builders, worker-output validators, reviewers, and future Agent99 policy consume these objects.

payload.answer: Each policy carries id, version, enabled, scope, prompt text, contract schema, and mechanical checks.

frequency.answer: Evaluated for every worker call whose worker kind and unit kind match the policy scope.

victim.answer: Consuming products and shared packages are harmed when warnings are missed and shared behavior is duplicated locally.

cost.answer: Adds policy serialization, versioning, scope matching, contract merging, UI editing, and fixture coverage.

cheaper_alternative.answer: Plain repo docs or stronger warnings are cheaper; rejected because the motivating incident showed warnings did not prevent duplication.

ecosystem_equivalent.answer: adopt: Agent99 has versioned capability policy objects; gap: orchestrator contracts are fixed schemas today.

invariants_contrast.statement: Contract extensions are declarative JSON over a closed verifier vocabulary and use the existing repair-retry path.

consumer.answer: The driver, validator, policy authors, reviewers, and workers consume the verifier vocabulary.

payload.answer: V1 carries path_exists, citation_exists, dir_listing_matches, non_empty, and enum; failed checks get one repair retry.

frequency.answer: Every in-scope worker output validation; exactly one repair retry on contract violation.

victim.answer: The operator and local machine are harmed if project config can inject code/shell or pass unverifiable claims.

cost.answer: Requires verifier dispatch, schema checks, path containment checks, repair messages, and tests for every verifier.

cheaper_alternative.answer: Arbitrary project plugins are more flexible; rejected because the closed vocabulary prevents code/shell injection.

ecosystem_equivalent.answer: gap: the orchestrator has repair-retry validation but no project extension registry or verifier vocabulary.

invariants_contrast.statement: The ledger records project_resolved once per run and project_safeguard_seen once per policy id/version shown to workers; run-scoped amendments win on conflict.

consumer.answer: Reviewers, fixers, seal halves, the operator, and future Persona/Brain surfaces consume these events to judge worker knowledge and precedence.

payload.answer: Events carry {project, work_area} and {policy_id, version, text[:300]}; amendments remain more specific later intent.

frequency.answer: Once at run init for project resolution, first-seen per safeguard id/version, and applied whenever safeguards conflict with amendments.

victim.answer: A reviewer or fixer is harmed if a worker is blamed for a safeguard absent from its prompt or if a later operator amendment loses precedence.

cost.answer: Adds ledger event types, dedup logic, prompt integration, version re-recording tests, and conflict ordering.

cheaper_alternative.answer: Do not ledger prompt exposure; rejected because amendment_seen already makes worker knowledge auditable.

ecosystem_equivalent.answer: adopt: current amendments record first-seen prompt exposure with clipped text.

invariants_contrast.statement: Skeletons and slice notes touching reusable surfaces must include a cited adopt/gap/reject reuse audit, and reviewers must contrast it.

consumer.answer: Planners, reviewers, fixers, source repos, and consuming products consume the audit decisions.

payload.answer: The audit carries package/source decisions with citations; reviewers carry per-package concur/dissent entries with their own citations.

frequency.answer: Planning and review time only; bounded by relevant reuse packages and audit rows.

victim.answer: Consuming products and LPC are harmed when existing shared behavior is duplicated locally.

cost.answer: Adds cross-repo reading, citation work, audit tables, reviewer contrast fields, and semantic review burden.

cheaper_alternative.answer: A stronger warning is cheaper; rejected because the prior prohibition failed.

ecosystem_equivalent.answer: gap: current prompts require Reuse Posture, not a per-package adopt/gap/reject audit with mechanical slots.

invariants_contrast.statement: Greenfield rule: there are zero existing project records, work areas, policies, or KV entries; no migrations, compat shims, tolerant readers, or deprecation cycles for nonexistent data.

consumer.answer: Reviewers, skeleton drafters, implementers, and fixture authors consume this rule when judging compatibility scope.

payload.answer: Compatibility means matching Agent99's current readers for future fusion, while the orchestrator writes the full new domain.

frequency.answer: Applies throughout this pre-milestone design and every implementation/review claim derived from it.

victim.answer: The operator and future implementer are harmed if review/fix work spends scope on migrations or tolerant readers for data that cannot exist.

cost.answer: Costs explicit fail-closed contracts and review discipline; saves migration, deprecation, and legacy-reader machinery.

cheaper_alternative.answer: Add broad compatibility padding; rejected because the milestone is new and the only real compatibility target is Agent99's current reader behavior.

ecosystem_equivalent.answer: gap: current orchestrator stores only the run workspace path and has no project/work-area/policy KV surface.
